# A pool read by its majority

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`a-pool-read-by-its-majority` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](a-pool-read-by-its-majority.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Taking what more than half the members read is a selection through the pooled coupling, separating no more than the pool; where more than half read alike on two histories it goes alike on them, though the fewer than half left may tell them apart: shares decide what it separates.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Counting the members a test holds of: counts under a weaker test are no more, alike tests count alike, and a test and its negation count every member once. (`Becoming.Web.holdsCount`, `Becoming.Web.toNat_le_of_imp`, `Becoming.Web.holdsCount_le_of_imp`, `Becoming.Web.holdsCount_congr`, `Becoming.Web.toNat_add_not`, `Becoming.Web.holdsCount_add_not`, `Becoming.ListTests.and_left`, `Becoming.ListTests.and_right`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
2. With each member reading through its own coupling, the majority reading selects through the pooled coupling; where more than half the members hold of both histories or fail of both, it goes alike on them. (`Becoming.Web.MajorityHolds`, `Becoming.Web.majority_through_all`, `Becoming.Web.majority_outvoted`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; a finite list of members, each reading a history as a truth value through its own coupling up to the step.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That any pool reads by its majority, or which members it holds.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
